feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but impact is reduced by repetition, limited quantified outcomes beyond one role, and a few style/grammar inconsistencies.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility through concrete platforms/tools: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Clarity, AI search, studio operations.  
- Writing is generally polished and audience-appropriate, with concise role summaries and relevant project examples.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes across roles: traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, production volume, efficiency gains, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; this makes the CV feel longer and less sharp than necessary.  
- Fix style consistency and minor wording issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; standardize serial comma usage, hyphenation (“member-facing,” “broadcast-quality,” “public-sector”), and date formatting (“Oct.”/“Sept.” vs other months). “Ranked among the top public universities…” under Education feels unnecessary and can be removed.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly dense and repeats themes covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with sharper outcomes and a tighter opening line.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more distinctive positioning line tied to public-sector platform leadership.
- Tighten the list of responsibilities into fewer, higher-impact phrases; “platforms, governance models and content operations” is solid but can be streamlined.
- Add scale or scope already evidenced elsewhere, e.g., enterprise web modernization for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, analytics, and editorial operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Builds the governance, content workflows, and multimedia systems that support complex, mission-driven communications, including AI-enabled search and user experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production” closely mirrors later skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with slightly tighter, more executive-level wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording for consistency: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership
- Clarify technical/value areas without repeating tools listed elsewhere: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration
- Refine sector focus for specificity: Public-sector advocacy communications
- Keep multimedia concise and senior-level: Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled… experiences,” and “multimedia production” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- This section also overlaps with Topline Skills; avoid listing tool-specific or channel-specific details already covered there.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise achievement, ideally with outcome language where possible.
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong but could be shortened for scanability.
- Standardize style and parallel structure across entries; e.g., start each with a strong verb and avoid repeating “Built/Developed.”
- If available, add 1 metric, audience, or scale marker to 1–2 projects to increase credibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in Work Experience.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider emphasizing projects not already described elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo leadership entry. Tighten it around what is new in the consulting remit and add outcomes or scale where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and cross-channel content operations as an external consultant.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics for organization-wide communications” instead of “Build and refine digital systems…”
- Consolidate overlapping web/CMS bullets into one stronger line: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, modular microsites, and member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for public-facing web properties.”
- Keep the most distinctive current work: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and user discovery experience.” Add metrics if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in the Director role.
- Broad references to web, email, social, and analytics may feel repetitive unless tied to new consulting-specific deliverables.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale signals, but it reads a bit list-like and overlaps with both the current consultant role and earlier NACo positions. Tighten around leadership outcomes, transformation, and enterprise-scale ownership.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and cross-channel strategy.”
- Combine channel oversight bullets and add outcomes where possible: email engagement, social growth, campaign performance, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Rephrase website bullet to emphasize transformation and scale: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make governance/analytics bullets more results-driven: note reporting speed, decision-making improvements, compliance, publishing consistency, or reduced operational friction.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, and analytics” overlaps with the current consultant role; keep this entry focused on executive ownership and delivered transformation.
- Email/newsletter and recurring video work overlap with the Associate Director role; emphasize expansion/leadership here, execution there.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination at this stage.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial operations.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.” / “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Rephrase vague bullets with stronger outcomes: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes linking communications, advocacy, and program staff” and “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency and turnaround.”
- Add metrics if available: newsletter open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, campaign response, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Improved workflows” and “editorial coordination” are repeated in both the 2022–2024 and consulting NACo roles.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the channel.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item is generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to recent leadership scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Editorial governance & operating models,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector advocacy messaging,” “Audience strategy & content planning.”
- Consider a more impact-oriented version: “Enterprise digital strategy • Editorial governance & content operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Audience-centered content strategy”
- Use “content operations” or “operating models” to reflect recent NACo leadership work more precisely than “systems.”
- Keep all items parallel noun phrases; avoid mixing leadership, messaging, and planning language inconsistently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than experience-based strengths like governance, analytics-informed strategy, or platform modernization.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to your NACo work rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Cut lower-priority platforms unless they are job-relevant targets; consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here if they already appear in Technical + IT.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Drupal platform builds and modernization for large public-facing sites” to echo recent impact without repeating metrics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full platform list.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies/Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a value-focused skills line. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing decision support/optimization would better match the impact shown in your 2022–present experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led grouping: “Digital analytics & optimization: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery”
- Replace vague terms with sharper business language: change “Leadership reporting” to “executive dashboards & decision support”
- Tighten “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX, and conversion/performance analysis” only if those are true/current strengths
- Consider revised version: “Digital analytics & optimization — GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery, KPI framework design, executive dashboards, SEO and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “KPI design” and “Leadership reporting” overlap with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies
- Tool names here duplicate the Director of Digital Media bullet; keep this section concise and let the work entry carry the proof of impact

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill cluster is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with broader “Multimedia & live event production” language elsewhere. Make it more specific to senior, recent capabilities and tools tied to the studio/event infrastructure you led.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Broadcast, Video & Hybrid Event Production**
- Replace with tighter, higher-signal bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera systems and studio operations
- Virtual event delivery and technical troubleshooting
- If space allows, add one stronger qualifier: **In-house studio buildout and production workflows**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close; combine to avoid repetition.
- This section overlaps with Core Competencies (“Multimedia & live event production”) and the NACo role about building an in-house studio, so keep this skills item tool-/execution-focused rather than repeating accomplishments.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” This item should either be tightened to a pure tools list or add light proficiency/context.

Suggested edit:
- Keep it as a concise platform-only line: Drupal (enterprise CMS) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put the strongest/recent platform first; Drupal should clearly lead given the recent 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Standardize naming for professionalism: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages.”
- If space allows, add level/context rather than more tools: Drupal (migration, governance, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; consider removing one or making this section strictly platform names while leaving capabilities in Topline Skills.
- Avoid adding CMS modernization, APIs, or automation here; those already appear elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current, implementation-focused, and selective.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop versioning (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more modern.
- Consider adding a brief qualifier if true: “for Drupal/CMS customization, tagging, automation, and lightweight serverless tools.”
- If space allows, prioritize tools tied to recent work and impact, e.g., “Cloudflare Workers” and “GitHub Actions” over older/basic items like “jQuery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.
- If you keep this section, use it for tool specificity only and let Topline Skills carry the broader summary.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already captured in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & collaboration systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the highest-signal tools first; lead with Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier since they best support your workflow/systems narrative.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clarity and stronger alignment with recent roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to outcomes in recent experience instead of expanding this list here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating those exact phrases.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are lower-impact than your recent enterprise systems work; trim if space is tight.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and undersells your email leadership in recent NACo roles. It should signal level of use and avoid repeating achievements already covered in Work Experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with a tighter, more credible list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses rather than features: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise campaign and journey management) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter campaigns)**
- Keep it platform-focused; let Work Experience carry audience size, newsletter frequency, and leadership impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that already appears in Director/Associate Communications Director entries.
- Don’t repeat “multi-channel communications” or strategy language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the NACo Director role. Tighten it to emphasize methods and outcomes, not just repeat platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools** or **Measurement & Experimentation**
- Replace “Dashboarding” with a more specific capability: **KPI reporting** or **Executive dashboards**
- Consider tighter phrasing: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI reporting**
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to impact via a project bullet rather than here, e.g., “Built analytics infrastructure and executive reporting to improve digital decision-making”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider removing one version or making this list tools-only and the Topline section capability-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating identical phrasing across sections.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to what was first built or launched in this period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and concrete outputs: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function.”
- Add sharper scope: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia production workflows during a major website refresh.”
- Make outputs more active and concise: “Produced livestreams, weekly video updates and other digital content supporting member communications and advocacy.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or team/process improvements; mention supervising “one digital media associate” only if that management detail is not stronger elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or piloting the format.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated throughout later roles; keep this lighter here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with one clear differentiator—the first podcast launch—but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize initiative, cross-functional coordination, and any concrete output.

Suggested edit
- Recast around the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and policy research projects for NACo programs while expanding digital storytelling support across content and multimedia initiatives.”
- Make the podcast the second sentence and lead with ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scale or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how it broadened member engagement.
- Remove vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production”; replace with specific deliverables such as articles, videos, audio segments, or campaign materials.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia production” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later entries better establish management and enterprise-level ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed capability list than a tight tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Video production and editing / Livestreaming / Studio operations” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as software + production systems, and tighten wording: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream studio systems • Podcast recording and post-production”
- Use consistent noun forms; avoid “workflows,” which is vague in a tools list. “Systems” or “operations” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add stronger tools/platform detail instead of generic production terms, e.g., streaming software, switchers, audio boards, or remote recording platforms.
- Only keep this section if it adds specificity beyond higher-level skills; otherwise shorten to the actual software stack.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” duplicates Topline Skills (“Livestreaming,” “Studio operations”).
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older experience; keep only if still relevant to current positioning.
